results.title: Dots UI: A React Library for Morphable Particle Interfaces
results.content: Dots UI is a new React library introduced to facilitate the creation of morphable particle interfaces. According to its Product Hunt listing, it enables developers to integrate particle-based UI elements that can dynamically change and morph, enhancing the interactivity and aesthetic appeal of web applications.

results.title: Dots UI — A React library for morphable particle interfaces ...
results.content: A particle library for React. Explore 171 morphing shapes across AI, productivity, media, commerce, and navigation. Use ready-made components, customize their appearance and behavior, or create your own shapes in Studio. Built for interactive interfaces, animated states, loaders, controls, visual effects, and UI that can transform from one form into another.

It would just be bad to do so. | | [...] |  |  | danielvaughn on July 2, 2024  | next (javascript:void(0))   I've worked as a freelancer on a couple of projects that used Ant Design, and personally I hated it. In one case I was working on a real estate platform, so I had to build a listing search page (similar to Zillow). This means you're rendering lots of little dots on the map, and on hover, each one will open a popover with the listing details. Using Ant Design brought this page to a standstill - massive performance issues, we're talking >1 second between frames. Turns out, it was rendering a unique portal element for every dot on the page, regardless of whether it was open or not.
